newsitem.title: USA: TCI says digital TV expansion top priority.
newsitem.headline: TCI says digital TV expansion top priority.

text.p: Tele-Communications Inc said on Tuesday it plans to offer its digital cable television service, All-TV, to over five million homes in 1997 and considers the service a top priority for the company.

Speaking at a PaineWebber media conference, Bernard Schotters, TCI's executive vice president of finance, said ALL-TV was a "perfect fit" for the company in the wake of recently announced cost cuts and layoffs.
"We have the infrastructure, we have the product, we have the technology and it does not induce leverage so it is a perfect fit given our financial situation," he said.
TCI, the nation's largest cable television operator, said last week it would cut 2,500 employees, or 6.5 percent of its work force, and review ways to cut costs and reduce its debt.
Schotters said the company's digital cable TV was "not a flavor of the month," but was central to the cable giant's strategy.

Investments in telephony and internet also are still important areas for the company, he said, but are much more capital intensive than digital cable television which offers an on-screen navigational guide to expanded movie choices and special-interest programs.
Camille Jayne, a TCI senior vice president, said the company plans to launch the service aggressively in March. It already is offered to Hartford, Conn., customers, she said.
She said the company would market the basic digital television package for a total of $34.99 a month and slightly enhanced packages for $49.99 a month.
